findings.governingReading: Shirou expects his original left arm to be restored beneath the cloth.
findings.explanation: The English drops which arm is at issue.

findings.highlight: I’ll die if I release it.
findings.governingReading: He concludes that unwrapping or undoing the cloth will kill him.
findings.explanation: “Release it” obscures the concrete action and can suggest releasing the arm or another object.

findings.highlight: I’ll slow down because of fear.
findings.evidenceJa: 恐怖で、切れ味が鈍くなる
findings.governingReading: Fear will dull his figurative cutting edge or sharpness.
findings.explanation: The English reduces the blade image to generic slowness.

findings.evidenceJa: そんな醜態は許されない
findings.governingReading: He refuses to permit himself such a disgraceful display.
findings.explanation: The English deletes the self-condemning image of disgrace and leaves an unspecified prohibition.

findings.highlight: Archer’s arm wasn’t transplanted onto me
findings.evidenceJa: アーチャーの腕を移植してまで生き延びたのは
findings.governingReading: He survived even at the cost of receiving Archer’s arm.
findings.explanation: The English makes the transplant itself the grammatical purpose and omits his survival.

findings.highlight: There are the mysterious enemies too.
findings.evidenceJa: 得体の知れない敵がいる
findings.governingReading: One unidentified, inscrutable enemy stands before them.
findings.explanation: The English turns the single unknown enemy into a known plural set.

findings.governingReading: He does not know how the arm’s dull ache will develop.
findings.explanation: The English removes the pain’s location and dull quality.
